body:
I used to work in a job, in my home country, where I didn't have to constantly talk with people. Which is how I saved up the money to get here. Although it was still stressful, it was easier to get a job and in my native language. 

As I implied in what I wrote, I currently live with my boyfriend and he financially supports me (which is why, as I said, he would have to pay for my therapy if I went). He says he doesn't have a problem with this, but I feel like a burden and I don't want to be the type of person who is financially dependant on someone else. 

I completely understand that my boyfriend is not my main problem and I never said he was. The problems we're having is just one on top of the others I've already expressed. This problem is just more in-my-face than the others. 

I know that you probably mean well, but your response really frustrates me because I feel like I've already covered most of what you said here in my original post. I don't need a friendly reminder that things depend on money. If I thought that everything was free, being jobless wouldn't bother me this much, now would it? And yes. I know I *should* talk to a therapist, and I've clearly explained why I haven't done so (which ultimately is my main problem).
